notes:
Account summary
- Helios Defense is pursuing Redwood Private for an on-prem, air-gapped deployment in a restricted enclave. Primary workloads are internal analyst summarization + doc search; early success criteria focuses on deterministic installs/upgrades and supply-chain assurances (signed offline bundles).
- They have strong internal security governance; they explicitly said they will not accept “we provide checksums” as sufficient. They want a signature verification step that fails closed and is auditable.

Key contacts / stakeholders (Helios)
- Security: Information Assurance lead + supply chain risk team (names withheld in CRM per request). They review key custody, signing algorithm, revocation/rotation plan, and audit evidence.
- Platform Ops: Kubernetes platform team responsible for air-gapped cluster maintenance and release intake process.
- Procurement: flagged that production purchase is contingent on a documented signing program and key ceremony evidence.

Redwood team / ownership
- Account owner: Markus Klein (enterprise coordination).
- SE: Colin O'Donnell (technical discovery + pilot execution support). PS: Bruno Silva engaged ad hoc for onsite/remote install automation support.
- Product: Vivek Kulkarni tracking GA criteria and ensuring Helios requirements map to signed bundle roadmap.
- Release Eng/Security: Connor O'Brien + Marcus Lin involved for signing pipeline and trust model questions.

Deployment constraints (confirmed)
- Air-gapped: no outbound egress from the cluster or installer host. All artifacts must arrive via approved removable media + internal scanning process.
- On-prem k8s: customer-managed cluster; they prefer Helm-based install but require that all charts/images/model artifacts are included in an offline bundle.
- Strict change control: upgrades can only occur in pre-approved windows; they want an explicit "what changed" manifest and a stable way to validate the bundle they received equals what Redwood shipped.
- Time: limited / controlled time sync; they raised concern about validity windows for signatures and “not yet valid” failures.

Requirements highlights (what Helios explicitly asked for)
- Signed offline bundles that include: installer binaries, Helm charts/manifests, container image references, runtime/model artifacts, and any dependency packages.
- Offline verification in the installer preflight (preferred) that blocks install/upgrade on:
  - signature mismatch
  - manifest hash mismatch
  - unknown/untrusted signing key
  - downgrade attempts (replay older signed bundle)
- Trust root management for air-gapped environments:
  - ability to update the installer trust store without internet access
  - clear procedure for key rotation, including overlap period with multiple keys
- Evidence package for security review:
  - key ceremony documentation
  - how keys are protected and who can sign
  - audit logs produced during verification (local) and how they can be exported to SIEM later

Pilot status
- Pilot started as “limited install + verify only” (no production traffic).
- Main pilot goal: validate the signed offline bundle workflow end-to-end (build -> transfer -> verify -> install) in Helios’ environment.
- Issues encountered:
  - Hash mismatch after transfer (see SUP-31892). Helios used a zip/unzip path that appeared to alter files (likely line endings / metadata). Provided guidance: avoid re-packing bundles; verify checksums on the transfer medium; use binary-safe tooling.
  - Signature verification failure due to installer version drift (older installer missing updated trust store behavior). We requested they standardize on the pilot installer version provided by SE.
  - Time skew concerns surfaced during testing: Helios asked for explicit diagnostics mode to print “bundle signing time”, “current system time”, and guidance if signature validity checks fail in an offline enclave.
